engagement_background.objective: Christianbook engaged Treya Partners to capture $655K–$1.2M of cost savings across indirect spend, strengthen enterprise value for its PE owner (Nonantum), and establish a best-in-class, data-driven procurement process that meets future business needs.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Project targets 8 main indirect categories—LTL/FTL freight, merchant processing fees, corrugated, packaging & shipping supplies, employee benefits, janitorial services, marketing software, and Ingram Book Group distribution—representing about $18 M in baseline spend (~$15 M addressable). Low-spend/low-opportunity areas may be dropped after initial review; core COGS, postage, real-estate and other non-addressable spend remain out of scope.
constraints_challenges: Long-standing incumbent relationships in packaging and LTL limiting willingness to change suppliers
Potential supplier non-responsiveness to data requests and competitive bidding exercises
Risk of side conversations or mixed messages to suppliers if Christianbook runs parallel procurement activity
Limited internal stakeholder bandwidth; need timely data provision and feedback to meet aggressive 5-6-month timeline
Incomplete line-item usage data for some high-spend vendors, requiring estimates or representative samples

procurement_environment.data_availability: 12-month AP data (Jun 2023–May 2024) with supplier, GL and limited commodity detail; contracts and line-item usage must be requested from key vendors.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: AP spend required manual mapping to Treya taxonomy; inconsistent vendor naming and gaps in historical usage data—especially where suppliers decline to provide details—necessitate baselining with partial or sampled data.
